Bug_Title: STI: Unneeded use of currentThread() call, to call interrupted() (STI_INTERRUPTED_ON_CURRENTTHREAD)
Bug_Details:
This method invokes the Thread.currentThread() call, just to call the
interrupted() method. As interrupted() is a static method, it is more
simple and clear to use Thread.interrupted().
 Thread.currentThread() interrupted() interrupted() Thread.interrupted()
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by using Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted() instead of the simpler and more direct Thread.interrupted(). This unnecessarily complicates the code and makes it less readable.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggers the bug by creating a thread that calls the `showBug` method of `InterruptedExample`. The thread is then interrupted, causing the `showBug` method to return `true` due to the unnecessary use of `Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted()` instead of `Thread.interrupted()`. The test case asserts that the result should be `false`, which causes the test to fail, demonstrating the bug.
Test_Run_Result: Runninng test will fail system because of infinite loop.

The bug involves the unnecessary use of Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted() instead of Thread.interrupted().
